# ez_spi  (`#include "ez_spi.h"`)

Hardware Abstraction Layer for SPI communication.

A HW driver is one SPI bus. A handle is one user of that bus, for example the driver of one device. The user opens a handle with ezSpi_Open(), which binds it to the HW driver by name and makes the bus ready in one step, and closes it with ezSpi_Close(). All the operations of a handle go through the HW driver registered with ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver().

Shared bus: several handles can be open on the same HW driver, for example one per device on the bus. They all share the configuration of the bus (clock, mode, bit order, frame size), which belongs to the board and not to the devices: the HW driver implementation puts it in ezSpiDriver::config before it registers the driver, and applies it in its initialize function. A port whose peripheral is already configured (for example by a generated start-up code) has no initialize function: an ezSpi_Open() then only binds the handle. The bus is initialized by the first ezSpi_Open() and released by the last ezSpi_Close(). The component counts the open handles. An ezSpi_Open() which fails leaves nothing behind, so the call can simply be repeated. The chip select of a device is not part of this component: the device driver controls it, for example with the GPIO component.

Concurrency: this component does not provide mutual exclusion for its calls. The caller must serialize the calls on the same HW driver. A call made while any handle of the same HW driver has an operation in flight returns EZ_DRV_STATUS_BUSY. A device which needs several transfers in a row (chip select low, command, data, chip select high) reserves the bus for the whole sequence with ezSpi_LockBus() and ezSpi_UnlockBus(), so that the handles of other tasks or modules cannot transfer in between. The HW driver provides the waiting (for example an RTOS mutex). Without an RTOS the lock is a try-lock.

Sync operations return when the transfer is done. Async operations return as soon as the transfer is started. The HW driver reports the end of an async operation by calling ezDriver_NotifyEvent(&hw_driver->base, EZ_DRV_EVENT_OP_DONE, EZ_SPI_EVENT_xxx, NULL, NULL), usually from its ISR. The driver is busy until then, and the handle callback is invoked after the driver is released, so it may start the next operation. A sync operation reports its result only through the return value. The HW function of a sync operation must NOT call ezDriver_NotifyEvent(): such events are dropped and the handle callback is not invoked. A HW driver which waits for an interrupt uses its own semaphore or flag for that.

No function of this component is ISR-safe. From an ISR, the HW driver only calls ezDriver_NotifyEvent().

Argument checking: this component only checks the handle. The buffers (NULL, size) and lengths (zero, too large) of the transfer functions are passed as they are to the HW driver, which is responsible for validating them, because only the HW driver knows what is valid for its peripheral (e.g. a zero-length transfer, or rx_length different from tx_length).

```c
typedef struct {
  EZ_SPI_MODE mode;  /* SPI mode (master/slave) */
  EZ_SPI_CLOCK_MODE clock_mode;  /* SPI clock mode */
  EZ_SPI_BIT_ORDER bit_order;  /* SPI bit order (MSB/LSB first) */
  uint32_t clock_frequency;  /* SPI clock frequency in Hz */
  uint8_t data_size;  /* Data size in bits (usually 8 or 16) */
} ezSpiConfig_t;
```
SPI bus configuration.

Member of ezSpiDriver (config). The HW driver implementation fills it before ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver() and applies it in its initialize function. The SPI component does not read, check or copy it. All handles open on the same HW driver share it. The HW driver decides which values it supports, and may ignore the structure when the peripheral is configured elsewhere.

```c
struct ezHwSpiInterface {
  void* driver_h;  /* Opaque pointer of the HW driver, passed to every function below */
  ezHwSpi_Initialize initialize;  /* Initialize the bus, for the first open handle (synchronous). NULL: already configured */
  ezHwSpi_Deinitialize deinitialize;  /* Release the bus, for the last closed handle (synchronous). NULL: nothing to release */
  ezHwSpi_Lock lock;  /* Take the bus, waits (blocking). NULL: no RTOS, ezSpi_LockBus() is a try-lock */
  ezHwSpi_Unlock unlock;  /* Give the bus back. NULL together with lock */
  ezHwSpi_TransferSync transfer_sync;  /* Transmit and receive at the same time (synchronous) */
  ezHwSpi_TransferAsync transfer_async;  /* Transmit and receive at the same time (asynchronous) */
  ezHwSpi_TransmitSync transmit_sync;  /* Transmit (synchronous) */
  ezHwSpi_TransmitAsync transmit_async;  /* Transmit (asynchronous) */
  ezHwSpi_ReceiveSync receive_sync;  /* Receive (synchronous) */
  ezHwSpi_ReceiveAsync receive_async;  /* Receive (asynchronous) */
};
```
HW API provided by the HW driver. Unused functions can be NULL.

A NULL function makes the matching ezSpi_xxx() return EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_INF_NOT_EXIST, except initialize, deinitialize, lock and unlock, which are optional: without initialize and deinitialize the peripheral is considered ready (already configured) and ezSpi_Open() only binds the handle. lock and unlock come as a pair, see ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver(). The HW functions are called with driver_h as the first argument.

The buffer pointers and lengths are not checked by the SPI component. Each HW function must validate them and return EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_ARG when they are not valid for the peripheral.

An async function returns EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK only if the transfer is started. The HW driver must then call ezDriver_NotifyEvent(&drv->base, EZ_DRV_EVENT_OP_DONE, EZ_SPI_EVENT_xxx, NULL, NULL) exactly once when it ends. If it does not start the transfer, it must return an error and must not call ezDriver_NotifyEvent(). See ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver() for an example.

```c
struct ezSpiDriver {
  struct Node ll_node;  /* Node to link to the list of HW drivers */
  struct ezDrvBase base;  /* Common data of driver: name, state and the handle in use */
  struct ezHwSpiInterface interface;  /* HW API, see ezHwSpiInterface */
  ezSpiConfig_t config;  /* Configuration of the bus, filled by the HW driver implementation before registration. Not used by the SPI component */
  uint8_t open_count;  /* Number of handles open on this bus. The bus is initialized while it is not 0. Reset to 0 on register */
  struct ezDrvHandle* volatile lock_owner;  /* Handle which holds the bus lock, NULL if free. Reset to NULL on register */
};
```
SPI HW driver. Provided by the HW driver implementation.

base.name must be set before ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver(). The driver is linked into the list of registered drivers, so its memory (static storage, no malloc) must stay valid while it is registered. config must be filled before ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver(). ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver() resets base.state, base.user, open_count and lock_owner, and keeps config.

```c
typedef struct {
  struct ezDrvHandle drv_handle;  /* Common handle, bound to a HW driver. Filled by ezSpi_Open() */
} ezSpiHandle_t;
```
SPI handle. Held by the user, one per user of the bus.

Must be zero-initialized (static storage, or memset) before the first ezSpi_Open(). Open it with ezSpi_Open() before use. The driver keeps a pointer to the handle in base.user while an operation is in flight and in lock_owner while the handle holds the bus, so the handle must stay valid until ezSpi_Close() returns EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK.

## Functions

### `ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver(struct ezSpiDriver *hw_driver);
```

Register a HW driver to the SPI component.

Called by the HW driver implementation, not by the application. The driver is reset to the idle, closed state: open_count is 0, base.state is 0 and base.user is NULL. It is then added to the list of HW drivers. base.name is compared with the names of the drivers already registered.

**Parameters**

- `hw_driver`: HW driver. base.name must be set and unique.

**Returns:** EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK on success, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_ARG if hw_driver or its name is NULL, the name is already registered, or only one of the lock and unlock functions is set.

- **Post:** base.state is 0, base.user is NULL and open_count is 0
- **Warning:** The driver list is changed without a lock. Call it from task context only, and not while another SPI call runs.
- **See:** ezSpi_SystemUnregisterHwDriver, ezHwSpiInterface
- ISR-safe: no
- Blocking: no

**Example**

```c
// HW driver side, at startup. The driver object is static (no malloc).
static struct ezSpiDriver spi0_drv;

EZ_DRV_STATUS RegisterSpi0(void)
{
    EZ_DRV_STATUS status = EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_GENERIC;

    spi0_drv.base.name = "spi0";                      // Must be unique
    spi0_drv.interface.driver_h = &spi0_regs;         // Given to every HW function
    spi0_drv.config.mode = EZ_SPI_MODE_MASTER;        // Bus configuration, applied by Spi0_Initialize()
    spi0_drv.config.clock_mode = EZ_SPI_CPOL0_CPHA0;
    spi0_drv.config.bit_order = EZ_SPI_BIT_ORDER_MSB_FIRST;
    spi0_drv.config.clock_frequency = 1000000U;
    spi0_drv.config.data_size = 8U;
    spi0_drv.interface.initialize = Spi0_Initialize;  // NULL if the peripheral is already configured
    spi0_drv.interface.deinitialize = Spi0_Deinitialize;
    spi0_drv.interface.lock = Spi0_Lock;              // Without an RTOS: NULL for lock and unlock
    spi0_drv.interface.unlock = Spi0_Unlock;
    spi0_drv.interface.transfer_sync = Spi0_TransferSync;
    spi0_drv.interface.transfer_async = Spi0_TransferAsync;
    spi0_drv.interface.transmit_sync = NULL;          // Unused: ezSpi_TransmitSync() returns EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_INF_NOT_EXIST
    spi0_drv.interface.transmit_async = NULL;
    spi0_drv.interface.receive_sync = NULL;
    spi0_drv.interface.receive_async = NULL;

    status = ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver(&spi0_drv);
    if(status != EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK)
    {
        return status;
    }
    return EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK;
}

// In the ISR of the SPI peripheral, when an async transfer ends
ezDriver_NotifyEvent(&spi0_drv.base, EZ_DRV_EVENT_OP_DONE, EZ_SPI_EVENT_CMPLT, NULL, NULL);
```

### `ezSpi_SystemUnregisterHwDriver`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_SystemUnregisterHwDriver(struct ezSpiDriver *hw_driver);
```

Unregister a HW driver from the SPI component.

Called by the HW driver implementation. The driver is removed from the list of HW drivers. base.state and base.user are not changed. The driver is refused while a handle is open on it, so no handle keeps a pointer to a driver which is gone.

**Parameters**

- `hw_driver`: HW driver registered earlier.

**Returns:** EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK on success, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_ARG if hw_driver is NULL, EZ_DRV_STATUS_BUSY if an operation is in flight on the driver, or a handle is still open on it (open_count is not 0).

- **Warning:** The driver list is changed without a lock. Call it from task context only, and not while another SPI call runs.
- **See:** ezSpi_SystemRegisterHwDriver, ezSpi_Close
- ISR-safe: no
- Blocking: no

### `ezSpi_Open`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_Open(ezSpiHandle_t *inst, const char *driver_name, ezDrvCallback callback, void *ctx);
```

Bind a handle to a registered HW driver and make the bus ready.

One call replaces "bind the handle" and "initialize the bus". The driver is taken for the call and released after it. If no handle is open on the driver yet and the HW driver has an initialize function, it is called. The bus is initialized with the configuration of the HW driver (ezSpiDriver::config). The caller does not pass a configuration: all users of one bus share it. If a handle is already open, the bus is already initialized and the HW driver is not called. Then the HW driver, the callback and the context are stored in the handle and the handle is counted as open.

If the HW initialization fails, the handle is left unbound, so the call can simply be repeated.

Whether it blocks depends on the HW driver. The SPI component adds no wait, but the HW function is synchronous, so it may block.

**Parameters**

- `inst`: Handle owned by the caller. Zero-initialized and not open. Must stay valid while open.
- `driver_name`: Name of the HW driver (base.name).
- `callback`: Called when an async operation of this handle ends. Can be NULL, then the end of the operation is not reported. Runs in the context of the HW driver, usually an ISR.
- `ctx`: User context, passed to callback as first argument. Can be NULL.

**Returns:** EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK on success, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_ARG if inst or driver_name is NULL, or the handle is already open, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_DRV_NOT_FOUND if no HW driver has the name, EZ_DRV_STATUS_BUSY if an operation is in flight on the driver, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_GENERIC if the maximum number of open handles (255) is reached, or the HW driver status otherwise.

- **Post:** On EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK the handle is open, the bus is initialized and the driver is idle. Otherwise the handle is not bound and the open count is unchanged.
- **Warning:** The callback runs inside ezDriver_NotifyEvent(), in the context of the HW driver, usually an ISR. It must not block.
- **Warning:** The SPI component is not a lock. Call it from one task, or let the upper layer serialize the calls on the same HW driver.
- **See:** ezSpi_Close, ezSpiDriver, ezHwSpiInterface, ezDrvCallback
- ISR-safe: no
- Blocking: yes

**Example**

```c
static ezSpiHandle_t spi0_handle;   // Static: must stay valid while open
static AppSpiCtx_t app_ctx;         // Passed to the callback, see ezSpi_TransferAsync()

EZ_DRV_STATUS OpenSpi0(void)
{
    EZ_DRV_STATUS status = ezSpi_Open(&spi0_handle, "spi0", OnSpiEvent, &app_ctx);
    if(status != EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK)
    {
        return status;               // Nothing is left bound: the call can be repeated
    }
    return EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK;
}
```

### `ezSpi_Close`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_Close(ezSpiHandle_t *inst);
```

Unbind a handle from its HW driver.

Clears hw, on_event and ctx of the handle and counts the handle as closed. If the handle holds the bus lock, the lock is released. When it was the last open handle of the driver, the deinitialize function of the HW driver is called, if it has one. Refused only when this handle has an operation in flight. An operation of another handle does not block it.

The handle is unbound even if the HW driver reports an error. The error is returned after the cleanup is finished. A handle which is not open is accepted and stays empty.

**Parameters**

- `inst`: Handle opened with ezSpi_Open(), or never opened.

**Returns:** EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK on success, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_ARG if inst is NULL, EZ_DRV_STATUS_BUSY if this handle has an operation in flight, or the HW driver status of deinitialize otherwise.

- **Post:** On EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK, and on a HW error, the handle is not open.
- **Warning:** The SPI component is not a lock. Call it from one task, or let the upper layer serialize the calls on the same HW driver.
- **See:** ezSpi_Open
- ISR-safe: no
- Blocking: yes

### `ezSpi_LockBus`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_LockBus(ezSpiHandle_t *inst, uint32_t timeout_millis);
```

Reserve the bus for a handle, for a sequence of several transfers.

The bus is shared by all the handles open on the HW driver. A device which needs several transfers in a row (for example chip select low, command, data, chip select high) locks the bus first, so that no other handle transfers in between.

With a lock function in the HW driver, the call waits up to timeout_millis for the bus (for example on an RTOS mutex) and returns EZ_DRV_STATUS_TIMEOUT if it is not free in time. Without one (no RTOS), nothing can wait: the call is a try-lock, timeout_millis is ignored and it returns EZ_DRV_STATUS_BUSY when another handle holds the bus. The caller retries later, for example in the next loop iteration.

While a handle holds the bus, every transfer of another handle returns EZ_DRV_STATUS_BUSY and the HW is not called. The lock is not recursive. It is independent of the busy state of a single operation: the holder can run any number of transfers.

**Parameters**

- `inst`: Open handle.
- `timeout_millis`: Longest time to wait for the bus. Ignored without a HW lock function.

**Returns:** EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK when the handle holds the bus, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_DRV_NOT_FOUND if the handle is not open, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_ARG if the handle already holds the bus, EZ_DRV_STATUS_BUSY if another handle holds the bus (no HW lock function), EZ_DRV_STATUS_TIMEOUT if the bus was not free in time, or the HW driver status otherwise.

- **Pre:** ezSpi_Open() succeeded for inst.
- **Post:** On EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK the handle holds the bus until ezSpi_UnlockBus() or ezSpi_Close().
- **Warning:** Task or main-loop context only, never from an ISR. Always unlock, also on error paths.
- **See:** ezSpi_UnlockBus
- ISR-safe: no
- Blocking: yes

**Example**

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS status = ezSpi_LockBus(&spi0_handle, 100U);
if(status != EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK)
{
    return status;
}
// ... GPIO chip select low, ezSpi_TransmitSync() or ezSpi_TransmitAsync() and wait, chip select high ...
status = ezSpi_UnlockBus(&spi0_handle);
if(status != EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK)
{
    return status;
}
```

### `ezSpi_UnlockBus`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_UnlockBus(ezSpiHandle_t *inst);
```

Give the bus back.

The lock is released first, then the unlock function of the HW driver is called, if it has one. Only the handle which holds the bus can unlock it.

**Parameters**

- `inst`: Open handle which holds the bus.

**Returns:** EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK on success, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_DRV_NOT_FOUND if the handle is not open, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_ARG if the handle does not hold the bus, or the HW driver status of unlock otherwise.

- **Pre:** ezSpi_LockBus() succeeded for inst.
- **Post:** The bus is free, also when the HW unlock reports an error.
- **See:** ezSpi_LockBus
- ISR-safe: no
- Blocking: no

### `ezSpi_TransferSync`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_TransferSync(ezSpiHandle_t *inst, const uint8_t *tx_data, size_t tx_length, uint8_t *rx_data, size_t rx_length, uint32_t timeout_millis);
```

Transmit and receive at the same time. Return when done.

Blocks the caller until the HW driver returns. timeout_millis is passed unchanged to the HW driver, which enforces it. The driver is taken for the call and released after the HW call returns, whatever the status.

**Parameters**

- `inst`: Registered handle.
- `tx_data`: Data to transmit.
- `tx_length`: Number of bytes to transmit.
- `rx_data`: Buffer for the received data.
- `rx_length`: Number of bytes to receive.
- `timeout_millis`: Timeout in milliseconds.

**Returns:** EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK on success, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_DRV_NOT_FOUND if the handle is not open, EZ_DRV_STATUS_BUSY if an operation is in flight on the driver, EZ_DRV_STATUS_ERR_INF_NOT_EXIST if the HW driver has no such function, or the HW driver status otherwise (e.g. EZ_DRV_STATUS_TIMEOUT).

- **Pre:** ezSpi_Open() succeeded for inst.
- **Warning:** The SPI component is not a lock. The caller must serialize the calls on the same HW driver.
- **Note:** The buffers and lengths are not checked by this component, the HW driver validates them. See ezHwSpiInterface.
- **See:** ezSpi_TransferAsync, ezSpi_Open
- ISR-safe: no
- Blocking: yes

**Example**

```c
uint8_t tx[2] = {0x9FU, 0x00U};
uint8_t rx[2] = {0U, 0U};
EZ_DRV_STATUS status = ezSpi_TransferSync(&spi0_handle, tx, sizeof(tx), rx, sizeof(rx), 100U);
if(status != EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK)
{
    return status;
}
```

### `ezSpi_TransferAsync`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_TransferAsync(ezSpiHandle_t *inst, const uint8_t *tx_data, size_t tx_length, uint8_t *rx_data, size_t rx_length);
```

Start to transmit and receive at the same time. Return immediately.

Returns as soon as the HW driver has started, or refused, the transfer. On EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK the transfer is running and the driver stays busy. The HW driver must then call ezDriver_NotifyEvent(&drv->base, EZ_DRV_EVENT_OP_DONE, EZ_SPI_EVENT_xxx, NULL, NULL) exactly once when the transfer ends. The callback of the handle is then called with that event_code. The driver is released before the callback runs, so the callback may start the next operation.

On any other status this call did not start a transfer, so no callback comes for it. The driver is released if this call had taken it. The HW driver must not call ezDriver_NotifyEvent() then.

**Parameters**

- `inst`: Registered handle.
- `tx_data`: Data to transmit.
- `tx_length`: Number of bytes to transmit.
- `rx_data`: Buffer for the received data.
- `rx_length`: Number of bytes to receive.

**Returns:** Same as ezSpi_TransferSync().

- **Pre:** ezSpi_Open() succeeded for inst.
- **Post:** On EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK the driver is busy until the end event is reported
- **Warning:** tx_data and rx_data must stay valid until the end event is reported. The SPI component does not copy them.
- **Warning:** The callback runs in the context of the HW driver, usually an ISR. It must not block.
- **Warning:** The SPI component is not a lock. The caller must serialize the calls on the same HW driver.
- **Note:** The buffers and lengths are not checked by this component, the HW driver validates them. See ezHwSpiInterface.
- **See:** ezSpi_Open, ezDriver_NotifyEvent, ezHwSpiInterface
- ISR-safe: no
- Blocking: no

**Example**

```c
typedef struct
{
    volatile bool rx_done;   // Set by the callback
} AppSpiCtx_t;

static AppSpiCtx_t app_ctx;     // Given to the callback as ctx
static uint8_t tx_buf[4];
static uint8_t rx_buf[4];

// Runs in the context of the HW driver, usually an ISR. Must not block.
static void OnSpiEvent(void *ctx, uint8_t event_code, void *param1, void *param2)
{
    AppSpiCtx_t *app = (AppSpiCtx_t *)ctx;
    if(event_code == EZ_SPI_EVENT_CMPLT)
    {
        app->rx_done = true;
    }
}

EZ_DRV_STATUS StartRead(void)
{
    EZ_DRV_STATUS status = ezSpi_TransferAsync(&spi0_handle, tx_buf, sizeof(tx_buf), rx_buf, sizeof(rx_buf));
    if(status != EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK)
    {
        return status;               // Not started: no callback will come
    }
    return EZ_DRV_STATUS_OK;         // Running: OnSpiEvent() gets the end event
}
```

### `ezSpi_TransmitSync`

```c
EZ_DRV_STATUS ezSpi_TransmitSync(ezSpiHandle_t *inst, const uint8_t *tx_data, size_t length, uint32_t timeout_millis);
```

Transmit data. Return when done.

Same rules as ezSpi_TransferSync(), without receive data.

**Parameters**

- `inst`: Registered handle.
- `tx_data`: Data to transmit.
- `length`: Number of bytes to transmit.
